title: add-benchmark-lab-performance-suites-reporting-pipeline-v127
author: Priya Nair
body: This PR adds a new set of benchmark-lab performance suites, representative workload runners, profiling baselines, and an end-to-end reporting pipeline. Motivation: provide automated nightly performance runs across a representative set of workloads (chat, longform generation, embeddings, and multi-turn streaming) and publish consolidated telemetry to the reporting stack so we can detect regressions and correlate kernel selection changes with throughput/latency impact. The change implements three pieces: 1) perf suites and workload runners under benchmark-lab/perf-suites/ (runner harness, workload definitions, and config presets); 2) profiling baselines and KV/prefix-cache sampling under benchmark-lab/profiling/; 3) a CI/workflow and reporting pipeline (CI workflow that schedules runs, a reporting job that uploads artifacts/metrics to our telemetry bucket, and a dashboard template). Checklist: - [x] Add workload runners for chat, embed, and longform (sampling + config presets) - [x] Add profiling baseline collectors and instrumentation (memory, kernel time, seq-latency histograms) - [x] Add reporting pipeline workflow (GitHub Actions + reporting job) - [x] Add dashboard and README/docs for running locally - [x] Add unit and integration tests for runner harness - [x] Add Linear links and release notes Notes on implementation: the runner harness is implemented in benchmark-lab/perf-suites/runner.py (Python) with pluggable workload definitions and a new artifact schema (bench-v1) for the reporting job. The reporting pipeline is a new workflow .github/workflows/bench-reporting-v127.yml that can be triggered manually or scheduled nightly. To keep the PR reviewable, the initial change uses a smaller default sample set; production sampling config will be increased in a follow-up once we verify storage and cost. Security considerations: all telemetry uploads go to an internal telemetry bucket with RBAC checks; no customer data is included in default workloads. Backwards compatibility: runners are additive and do not change runtime behavior for serving. See release_notes field for user-visible items.
commits: Initial runner harness and workload definitions (benchmark-lab/perf-suites)
Add profiling baselines and sampling hooks (benchmark-lab/profiling)
Add GitHub Actions workflow for scheduled reporting and manual triggers (.github/workflows/bench-reporting-v127.yml)
Fix telemetry schema mismatch and update uploader to bench-v1 format
Update docs and add dashboard template (docs/benchlab.md, dashboards/bench-v127.json)
review_comments: Liam Chen: Can we avoid uploading raw stack traces to the telemetry bucket? Suggest redacting before upload.
Priya Nair: Addressed - uploader now strips stack traces and retains only symbolized error classes in bench-v1 schema.
Maya Patel: The workflow currently runs on ubuntu-latest; do we need an explicit GPU runner label for dedicated profiling?
Priya Nair: Added optional 'gpu-runner' matrix config and documented how to opt-in for dedicated runs in the README.
Diego Martinez: Tests failing intermittently on e2e due to timing; can we add retries to the harness?
Priya Nair: Added retry logic with exponential backoff for transient infra failures; re-ran CI and tests are stable now.
release_notes: Added benchmark-lab performance suites and nightly reporting pipeline (v127). Includes workload runners for chat, embeddings, and longform, profiling baselines, and dashboard templates. No breaking changes.
summary: Nightly perf suites + profiling baselines + reporting pipeline to detect regressions and centralize performance telemetry.
